title: Cervical Artery Dysfunction and Upper Cervical Instability
lead: A safety chapter. Learn to recognise rare but dangerous conditions before treating the neck.
case: A 40-year-old has new severe right neck pain after a fall while playing cricket, and now a drooping right eyelid.
working: Cervical Artery Dysfunction and Upper Cervical Instability

differentials.name: Mechanical neck pain
differentials.key: Pain changes with movement and posture, no neurological signs

differentials.name: Migraine
differentials.key: History of similar attacks, aura, photophobia

differentials.name: BPPV
differentials.key: Brief spinning vertigo with position, no other neurological signs

differentials.name: Cervicogenic headache
differentials.key: One-sided, provoked by neck movement, positive flexion-rotation test

qa: Can a negative positional test clear a patient for manipulation? No. Accuracy is uncertain; history and clinical reasoning matter most.
List the 5 Ds. Dizziness, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, drop attacks.
A 40-year-old has new severe right neck pain after a fall while playing cricket, and now a drooping right eyelid. What do you suspect? Possible carotid dissection with Horner syndrome. Emergency.
Why is rheumatoid arthritis important for neck treatment? It can weaken upper cervical ligaments, causing instability.
What is your safest default when you are unsure? Avoid high-velocity or end-range techniques, use exercise and gentle methods, and seek medical advice.

fields.Purpose: Check for excessive forward movement of C1 on C2
fields.Therapist position: Beside patient; one hand on the forehead, thumb and index finger of the other hand pinching the C2 spinous process
fields.Action: Gently push the forehead backward while stabilising C2
fields.Positive: A sliding movement or "clunk", with relief of symptoms provoked by flexion
fields.Next step: Stop; no manual therapy; urgent medical review
fields.Caution: Do not perform after acute trauma; imaging first

fields.Action: Stabilise C2 by holding its spinous process; gently side-bend the head
fields.Normal: Immediate C2 movement (the ligament pulls C2 along)
fields.Positive: Delayed C2 movement or excessive head side-bend

redFlags.Finding: New severe unusual neck pain or headache with any of the 5 Ds, 3 Ns or ataxia
redFlags.Immediate action: Stop; emergency services; note the time of onset

redFlags.Finding: Horner syndrome, visual loss, one-sided weakness
Positive Sharp-Purser or alar test, bilateral limb paraesthesia
Very high blood pressure with headache

manualNotes: Physiotherapy does not treat dissection or instability directly. The physiotherapist's role is recognition, referral and later rehabilitation after medical management.
After medical clearance, rehabilitation is gentle, active, and avoids end-range or high-velocity techniques in the cervical spine.
Patients with rheumatoid arthritis or Down syndrome should not receive upper cervical manipulation without specialist clearance.
